A secondary group may need its own short explanation if the course plays a different role in that group.
A secondary group’s short explanation may describe how the course fits a pathway or a career interest.
The primary placement should remain the main source of truth.
If there is a real difference in audience or context, a fuller summary or a different link is appropriate.
Any fuller summary or different link should be limited to avoid conflicting information.
The system shall separate referral source segmentation by audience and context when needs differ enough to change the messaging or next step.
The system shall provide a different path for a high-school student seeking encouragement than for a parent, counselor, or older visitor seeking factual details.
The system shall allow grouping of two entry sources together when they lead to the same kind of intent.
The system shall group referral sources only when the grouping helps tailor the experience and not merely for the sake of creating segments.
The system shall use the entry point as a cue for determining audience context.
The system shall distinguish audience context based on whether the user entered through a student-facing page, a career story, or informational course details.
The system shall rely on the content the user is already viewing and on whether the user appears to need encouragement versus straight facts when age is not obvious.
The system shall use a friendly and simple tone for pages about getting started.
The system shall use more precise terminology on course planning pages.
The system shall default to clear and approachable language when it cannot determine the audience context.
